1  :JUDGMENT:
This claim petition emanates in respect of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner by name Shajahan in respect of the Road Traffic Accident dated 22.03.2020.
2.

Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
That on 22.03.2020 at about 12.30 a.m., when the petitioner was driving his Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.AP-03- TC-517 from Murukumbattu towards Chittoor slowly, cautiously on the correct side of Chittoor - Putalapattu road and when he reached near Doddipalli Railway Bridge, at that time, respondent's Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AG-4838 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle) came from opposite SCCH 15 3 MVC No.553/2021 direction at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's autorickshaw, as a result,
petitioner got caught inside the auto and sustained grievous injuries.
3. Immediately, after the accident petitioner was shifted to government hospital, Chittooor, after first aid treatment he was shifted to CMC hospital, Vellor, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
Hence, the petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
4. In pursuance of service of notice issued to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.

The Respondent No.2 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
The respondent No.2 admitted that it has issued policy to the offending vehicle in favour of the respondent No.1.
Without prejudice the liability of the respondent No.2 if any is subject SCCH 15 4 MVC No.553/2021 to the validity of driving license and terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Further offending vehicle was not having valid permit and fitness certificate as on the date of alleged accident.

The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied that the accident was caused by rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and denied involvement of its vehicle in the alleged accident.
The petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

5. Vide order dated 24.03.2022 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01- S. Shajahan vs Kabir Ahmed Nazeer on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157861626/

3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
4) What Order or Award?

RECASTED ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 22.03.2020 at about 12.30 a.m. near Doddipalli Railway Bridge, Chittoor -
Putalapattu Road, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AG- 4838 by its driver?
6.

In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 18 SCCH 15 6 MVC No.553/2021 documents and respondent No.2 got examined three witnesses as RW.1 to 3 and relied upon Ex.R1 to 5 documents.
7.
Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
Recasted Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.

It is the contention of the petitioner that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA- 01-AG-4838/offending vehicle.

In this regard the petitioner has got examined himself as PW.1 and in his chief-examination he has deposed that on SCCH 15 7 MVC No.553/2021 22.03.2020 at about 12.30 a.m. the petitioner was going towards Chittoor from Murukumbattu driving his Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TC-517 slowly, cautiously on the correct side of Chittoor - Putalapattu road and when he reached near Doddipalli Railway Bridge, at that time, offending vehicle came from opposite direction with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's autorickshaw, as a result, he was caught inside the auto and sustained grievous injuries.
10.
The petitioner in support of his claim has in addition to describing the course of the accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to 6 documents.

Ex.P1 is the FIR which discloses that the case has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offenses under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC on the basis of the complaint given by one Babulal S/o Salim Saheb as per Ex.P2 on 23.03.2020.
Hence there is no delay in lodging the complaint.
Further Ex.P3 is the statement given by the SCCH 15 8 MVC No.553/2021 petitioner to the police regarding the manner of the accident.

The spot sketch produced at Ex.P4 discloses that the width of the road is about 60 feet proceeding from Tirupati - Chittoor road and the spot of the accident is at the extreme right side from north towards sought of the said road near the bridge.
The documents discloses that it is head on collusion and the offending vehicle came from the opposite direction from the front side and dashed the auto of the petitioner, resulting in the accident.
Ex. P6
- wound certificate discloses that the petitioner has sustained injuries due to the impact of the accident.

Ex.P7 is the charge sheet filed after completion of investigation against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offense under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and under Sec.134(a) (b) of MV Act and the charge sheet documents discloses that the driver of the offending vehicle / car was proceeding towards Tirupati side and dashed the auto and the inmates of the auto sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, based on these documents SCCH 15 9 MVC No.553/2021 it is evident that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

11. As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and in his cross-examination he has deposed that the accident took place at Doddipalli Railway Bridge and he was driving the auto at the time of the accident.
He has deposed that the car came from the opposite direction and dashed from the front side, resulting in the accident.
In support of the PW.1 also produced 6 photos marked as Ex.P13 to show the manner of the accident.

Except suggesting that the accident took place due to the negligence of PW.1 and the photos produced are created, nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence or rashness on the part of petitioner.
The petitioner has clearly and categorically deposed about the manner of the accident.
The oral testimony of PW.1 has stood unrebutted and PW1 has withstood the cross- SCCH 15 10 MVC No.553/2021 examination of Respondent No.2.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
PW.1 has also denied the suggestion imputing the cause of the accident to be due to his negligence.

The fact that the rider of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and under Sec.134(a) (b) of MV Act itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.

The certified copies of FIR,

sentences.text: In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 in the above accident.

In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence of driver, driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

Hence, Recasted issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioner and in the 'Affirmative'.
SCCH 15 11 MVC No.553/2021 12. Issue No.2: In view of the findings on issue No.1 in favour of petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
The computation of compensation will have to be decided separately under various heads.
13. MEDICAL OR TREATMENT EXPENSES:

As far as the medical expenses are concerned the petitioner has produced Ex.P6 - wound certificate which discloses that the petitioner has sustained injuries due to the impact of the accident and he has sustained right shaft fracture femur and left mid third and clavicle fracture and in addition produced Ex.P8 - Discharge summary of Christian Medical college, Vellore which discloses that the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient on 22.03.2020 and discharged on 24.03.2020 and he has sustained two fractures.
The petitioner has produced Ex.P9 - medical bills of Christian Medical College, Vellore and produced Ex.P16 - case sheet of Christian Medical College, Vellore.
As far as the medical bills are concerned except suggestion that the medical bills are created nothing much is SCCH 15 12 MVC No.553/2021 elicited to disprove the authenticity of the said bills.
In addition no evidence is adduced to show that these bills are reimbursed.
Hence petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.38,121/- under this head.
14. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

As per the medical documents the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and Ex.P6 discloses that the petitioner has sustained right shaft fracture femur and left mid third and clavicle fracture and it is stated in the petition that injuries sustained and physical impairment has caused unbearable pain and petitioner cannot do any work as prior to the accident.
It is not possible to ascertain quantum of compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc., which he actually suffered due to the accidental injuries.

Keeping in view the trauma and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.30,000/- is awarded to him towards pain and sufferings.
SCCH 15 13 MVC No.553/2021 Thus, he is awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
15. LOSS OF ACTUAL EARNINGS:
In his evidence PW.1 has submitted he was aged about 32 years and he was working as an auto driver and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
In this regard he has not produced any documents to prove the actual income and avocation of the petitioner.

Since, there is no satisfactory evidence to prove the said income and avocation of the petitioner it would be proper to assume the monthly earnings of the petitioner as per the notional income as on the date of the accident.
As per the minimum wages chart the income for the said avocation for the relevant period is ranging between 14,000 to 15,000/- and hence the notional income is taken as Rs.14,500/- p.m.

Taking into consideration that the petitioner due to the injuries might not have been in a position to work for at least 3 months hence, as such the petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.14,500 X 3 =

SCCH 15 14 MVC No.553/2021 16. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS DUE TO DISABILITY:

The petitioner has claimed in his affidavit he has permanent disability and as per the evidence of PW.2 his impairment is not progressive and will not improve in future and hence it is submitted by the petitioner that he cannot pursue his work as before the accident.

As far as the disability is concerned the petitioner has got examined PW.3 - Orthopedic Surgeon and in his evidence he has deposed that the petitioner has underwent CRIF with IMIL nailing in CMC hospital, Vellore and he has restricted range of movements of knee and hip and pain and has difficulty in cross leg sitting,
squatting and the right femur fracture united with implant in situ.
He has deposed that he has assessed the disability as per gazette notification and the petitioner has disability for limbs at 47% and whole body disability is 15.66%.

PW.3 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and in his cross-examination he has deposed that the fracture is united and he has not seen the past X-ray SCCH 15 15 MVC No.553/2021 of the petitioner.
PW.3 has denied that he has not assessed the disability as per telescopic formula and denied that there are chances of reduction in disability.
He has deposed that petitioner has do his day to day activities with some difficulty.
Except the said suggestion nothing much is elicited to disprove the disability assessed by him.

17. As far as functional disability is concerned it is submitted by the petitioner that he is working as an auto driver and taking into consideration the disability of the petitioner he certainly will have to continue his avocation with some difficulties.
The monthly income of the petitioner is already assessed at Rs.14,500/- at the relevant time.
As far as, age of the petitioner at the time of the accident is concerned on perusal of the petitioner's Aadhaar card Ex.P10 the date of birth of the petitioner is 01.01.1988.

Going by the same, the age of petitioner as on date of accident i.e.,
22.03.2020 was around 32 years.

Therefore, in view of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and others Vs. SCCH 15 16 MVC No.553/2021 Delhi Corporation and another (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the judgment dated 31.10.2017 given in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, the multiplier of '16' is held applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of petitioner arising out of his above disability.

23. Regarding Liability:

As far as the liability is concerned the respondent No.2 has got examined its legal officer as RW.1 and in his evidence he has deposed that the vehicle of respondent No.1 is insured with respondent No.2 for the period 15.12.2019 to 14.12.2020 vide policy no.418005/31/20/021048.

However, it is subject to terms and conditions of the policy it is submitted by RW.1 that the respondent No.1 was not having valid DL as on the date of the accident and there was no valid Permit and FC as on the date of the accident and hence there is breach of policy conditions.

24. In support of the same RW.1 produced copy of insurance policy at Ex.R2 and also the permit extract at Ex.R3 discloses that it is copy of the permit and as per the permit, it is valid from 22.12.2016 to 21.12.2021.

In order to further SCCH 15 20 MVC No.553/2021 substantiate the defense of the respondent insurance company the respondent has got examined RW.2 - FDA, RTO,
HSR Layout and he has produced Ex.R5 which is canceled permit and stated that permit is canceled on 01.06.2022 and prior the vehicle had Karnataka State Permit and on the request of the owner the permit is canceled.
RW.2 is cross-

examined by the counsel for the petitioner and he has admitted that as on the date of the accident i.e., 22.03.2020, the permit was in force and he has also admitted when the vehicle goes from one state to another state, the temporary permit is obtained at the border.
25.
RW.1 in his cross-examination has deposed that they have issued notice to the owner and there was no reply from the owner.
He has admitted that the car is LMV vehicle and the DL to the car is valid till 2025.

Further, the investigation officer Nagari Urban, PSI, Chittoor is examined and in his evidence he has deposed that offending vehicle is yellow board commercial passenger vehicle which requires compulsory SCCH 15 21 MVC No.553/2021 permit and permit was not produced at the time of investigation.
He has deposed that permit is only obtained to travel within Karnataka State and the respondent has not produced any temporary permit to travel in Chittoor district, Andhra Pradesh.
26. As far as the permit is concerned it is admitted that the charge sheet is not filed for 'no valid permit or DL'.
The document Ex.R5 discloses that as on the date of the accident the offending vehicle had permit through out Karnataka state from 22.12.2016 to 21.12.2021.
Hence, the only ground raised by the insurance company is that there was no temporary permit obtained to travel in the state of Andhra pradesh.

However, RW.2 has admitted that temporary permit is obtained at the border of the state and RW.3 in his cross- examination has admitted that when the vehicle goes to S. Shajahan vs Kabir Ahmed Nazeer on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157861626/

sentences.text: Since the offending vehicle was commercial vehicle only if the temporary permit is obtained the vehicle will SCCH 15 22 MVC No.553/2021 be permitted to pass at the border.
RW.1 has admitted that the temporary permit particulars have not been obtained from the RTO.
Hence, it can be considered that there is only a deviation in the permit and it is not a case that there was non existence permit.
In the course of investigation, no charge sheet is filed for violation of permit and neither the investigation officer has investigated with the RTO about the temporary permit obtained at the border.
The respondent No 1 in this case has remained and has not adduced any evidence nor produced any document to show existence of temporary permit to ply in Chittoor district.

Hence there is certainly violation of permit and is a breach of the policy conditions which can exonerate the insurance company from indemnifying the insured respondent No 1.
27.

Be it as it may the evidence discloses that it is not a case of non existence of permit but it is case of deviation of the route or violation of the terms of permit and hence it is not a breach which has a fundamental impact on the occurrence of SCCH 15 23 MVC No.553/2021 the accident or which would make the contract void.
Hence violation of the terms of the permit shall entitle the insurance company a right to seek recovery of the compensation paid to the claimants from the owner of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: There is no doubt that the respondent No 2 has proved that there is breach of policy conditions since there was no permit to ply in Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh.
There is no doubt that the liability has to be fastened on the owner/respondent No 1 and the respondent No 2 will have to be exonerated of their liability.

Admittedly as per the conditions under the policy the vehicle must be used only SCCH 15 25 MVC No.553/2021 under a permit however the Motor vehicles Act being a benevolent piece of legislation a duty is cast on the insurance company to satisfy the award against the persons insured in respect to the third party risks and the insurance company is entitled to defend the claim interalia on the ground that there has been a breach of the condition of the policy as the offending vehicle was being used in a place not allowed under the permit.
29. The learned counsel for the insurance company would contend that the accident having occurred after the amendment and hence the principle of pay and recovery is not applicable.
However there is no clear provision by way of amendment to indicate that the said principle is no longer in existence or expressly excluded.
If the legislature intended to wipe out the said principle it would have made a clear provision to that effect.

Furthermore the contract of insurance is between the insurer and the insured and the intention of making statutory third party insurance is to compensate the SCCH 15 26 MVC No.553/2021 road accident victims and their remedy cannot be abridged on the ground on of breach of policy conditions.
Hence they are entitled to obtain compensation from respondent no 2 who in turn will have to recover the same from the insured.
Hence the Respondent No.1 being owner of the vehicle is liable to pay the compensation.
However Respondent No.2 will have to deposit the compensation amount and thereafter recover the same from Respondent No.1.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 is "Partly in the Affirmative".
30. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 and 2 and under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,07,595/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% SCCH 15 27 MVC No.553/2021 p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.

However, the Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest as stated above within 60 days from the date of the Award and thereafter recover the same from the Respondent No.1 through due process of law.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E-payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The fact that the rider of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and under Sec.134(a) (b) of MV Act itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence of driver, driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Going by the same, the age of petitioner as on date of accident i.e.,
22.03.2020 was around 32 years.
22. Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.
LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has SCCH 15 19 MVC No.553/2021 been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.
Since the offending vehicle was commercial vehicle only if the temporary permit is obtained the vehicle will SCCH 15 22 MVC No.553/2021 be permitted to pass at the border.
RW.1 has admitted that the temporary permit particulars have not been obtained from the RTO.
Hence, it can be considered that there is only a deviation in the permit and it is not a case that there was non existence permit.
In the course of investigation, no charge sheet is filed for violation of permit and neither the investigation officer has investigated with the RTO about the temporary permit obtained at the border.
The respondent No 1 in this case has remained and has not adduced any evidence nor produced any document to show existence of temporary permit to ply in Chittoor district.
Hence there is certainly violation of permit and is a breach of the policy conditions which can exonerate the insurance company from indemnifying the insured respondent No 1.
27.
Be it as it may the evidence discloses that it is not a case of non existence of permit but it is case of deviation of the route or violation of the terms of permit and hence it is not a breach which has a fundamental impact on the occurrence of SCCH 15 23 MVC No.553/2021 the accident or which would make the contract void.
Hence violation of the terms of the permit shall entitle the insurance company a right to seek recovery of the compensation paid to the claimants from the owner of the offending vehicle.
There is no doubt that the respondent No 2 has proved that there is breach of policy conditions since there was no permit to ply in Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh.
There is no doubt that the liability has to be fastened on the owner/respondent No 1 and the respondent No 2 will have to be exonerated of their liability.
Admittedly as per the conditions under the policy the vehicle must be used only SCCH 15 25 MVC No.553/2021 under a permit however the Motor vehicles Act being a benevolent piece of legislation a duty is cast on the insurance company to satisfy the award against the persons insured in respect to the third party risks and the insurance company is entitled to defend the claim interalia on the ground that there has been a breach of the condition of the policy as the offending vehicle was being used in a place not allowed under the permit.
However there is no clear provision by way of amendment to indicate that the said principle is no longer in existence or expressly excluded.
If the legislature intended to wipe out the said principle it would have made a clear provision to that effect.
Furthermore the contract of insurance is between the insurer and the insured and the intention of making statutory third party insurance is to compensate the SCCH 15 26 MVC No.553/2021 road accident victims and their remedy cannot be abridged on the ground on of breach of policy conditions.

30. Issue No.3:
In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 and 2 and under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,07,595/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% SCCH 15 27 MVC No.553/2021 p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest as stated above within 60 days from the date of the Award and thereafter recover the same from the Respondent No.1 through due process of law.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E-payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
